html:
The Salmon River people lived around the mouth of the Salmon River on the central Oregon coast, near today's Lincoln City. They are usually counted as a southern group of the Tillamook, speakers of a Coast Salish language, and are sometimes called the Nechesne.

They fished salmon and gathered shellfish along the estuary. After the treaties of the 1850s, the survivors of disease and war were placed on the Coast Reservation, and their descendants belong today to the Siletz and Grand Ronde tribes. Little else is recorded about them as a separate people.
